description: A tree of terra firme, slopes, 30-40 m tall (to 50 m). Straight cylindrical bole 75-115 cm diameter (Useful Tropical Plants). Climax species that dominates canopies on well-drained slopes (English Wikipedia). Fruit: round, juicy, fleshy fruit up to 5 cm diameter with edible seeds.

notes: Template shorea_leprosula: an emergent: a buttressed clear bole under an umbrella crown (light red meranti). NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): crown width (the template's ratio); crown depth (the template's); leaf size (the median of the research records' sourced simple leaves, 0.17 m); leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green); bark texture (the template's). Research notes: Height: Spanish Wikipedia up to 50 m; Titi Conservation Alliance up to 40 m; English Wikipedia and Useful Tropical Plants 30 m. typical [30,40] spans those maxima, not a measured typical. Leaves: simple, alternate, large, with a very acute apex; hairy stipules enclose the developing leaves (es Wikipedia, src 3); no sizes or colours found. Phenology is from the Titi Conservation Alliance (central and south Pacific Costa Rica, Quepos to Osa): flowers all year, fruit mainly April-June. Flower colour: cream or yellowish (es Wikipedia); small and white (src 3). Fruit size 'up to 5 cm' from es Wikipedia, which also says many species eat the fruit avidly without naming them. Evergreen per Useful Tropical Plants ('Evergreen forest formations below 400 m'). Shade-tolerant per English Wikipedia. Src 3 names 'sainos' and 'chanchos de monte'; the scientific names are my mapping of those Costa Rican names (collared and white-lipped peccary). Domestic animals: cattle eat leaves and branch tips, pigs the fruit (en Wikipedia), not listed. No Corcovado-specific fauna records found. Costa Rican trees are subsp. occidentale per HVAA image captions (not verified in a treatment). Flora Costaricensis and the Golfo Dulce field guide (Stapfia 78) were blocked (403).
